advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Match the push/PR caller via parsed `jobs.<name>.uses == reusable` instead of a raw-text substring so a comment mention cannot satisfy the caller requirement.
evidence: The check is substring-based over raw file text rather than a parsed `jobs.<name>.uses` lookup, so it cannot distinguish an executable `uses:` from a comment that happens to contain `uses: ./.github/workflows/_X.yml`.
advisory.finding: The push/PR caller-existence check tests `f"uses: {reusable}" in path.read_text(...)` against the whole file text, so a mention of the reusable path inside a YAML comment or other prose (not an actual `uses:` key invoking it) would satisfy the 'a push/PR lane calls this reusable' assertion.
scenarios: A workflow comment documents the reusable path (e.g. 'this mirrors uses: ./.github/workflows/_optionality.yml') while the actual job wiring was removed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Parse each candidate workflow with yaml.safe_load and check `any(j.get("uses") == reusable for j in doc.get("jobs", {}).values())` rather than a substring over `read_text()`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md:270-271 which still references the deleted `_SHARED_GATE_SIGNATURES`/`_DOCUMENTATION_GATE_SIGNATURES` dicts (and stale line citations).
evidence: reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md:271: "`_DOCUMENTATION_GATE_SIGNATURES` (`:84`) back to the scripts on disk."
advisory.finding: The documentation at reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md references `_SHARED_GATE_SIGNATURES` and `_DOCUMENTATION_GATE_SIGNATURES`, both deleted from tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py by this diff; the doc also cites now-stale source line numbers (`:66`/`:84`), so these are dangling references not updated in the diff.
scenarios: A reader follows the mirror-inventory caveat to the named dicts and finds they no longer exist in test_ci_workflow_parity.py.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `_verified_lane_reusable_jobs()` is non-empty (and ideally matches the expected count) so the parametrized parity rule cannot pass vacuously when zero jobs are collected.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:676-680: `return sorted((name, job["uses"]) for name, job in jobs.items() if str(job.get("uses", "")).startswith("./.github/workflows/_"))`
ABSENCE: no test asserts `_verified_lane_reusable_jobs()` returns a nonzero/expected count (commit says '6 today'); an empty list silently yields no parametrized nodes rather than a failure.

The deleted real-tree assertions (test_real_repo_verify_gate_is_in_parity / test_real_repo_check_main_returns_zero in test_verify_gate_parity.py) were the definite-verdict checks against the committed tree; the new parametrized check replaces per-gate wiring but can degrade to zero cases.
blocking.finding: The rewritten parametrized test derives its parameter set at collection time from `_verified_lane_reusable_jobs()`; if that helper yields an empty list (gerrit-verify.yaml renamed/moved, its `jobs` shape changes, or no job matches the `./.github/workflows/_` prefix), pytest generates ZERO test instances and the entire Verified-lane parity rule passes vacuously. A 'rule never ran' outcome is indistinguishable from 'ran and all jobs are wired correctly'.
scenarios: Someone renames gerrit-verify.yaml or restructures its jobs so none carry a `uses: ./.github/workflows/_*.yml` key.
A refactor changes the reusable-path prefix convention, so `startswith("./.github/workflows/_")` matches nothing.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a standalone (non-parametrized) test that asserts `len(_verified_lane_reusable_jobs()) >= 1` (or == the known count) so an empty collection reddens instead of silently passing.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a non-emptiness/expected-count guard so test_optionality_contract_gates_the_verified_path fails (not silently collects zero cases) when _verified_lane_reusable_jobs() discovers no reusable Verified jobs.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:684: `("job", "reusable"), _verified_lane_reusable_jobs(), ids=...` — argvalues computed from the live workflow at import time
tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:676-680: the comprehension filters `job.get("uses","").startswith("./.github/workflows/_")`; a rename off that prefix yields `[]`

ABSENCE: no assertion anywhere (searched `_verified_lane_reusable_jobs`) that the discovered list is non-empty / equals the expected 6 jobs; an empty parametrize set is not collected as a failure, so the contract fails open

Commit message states '6 today' and that this 'replaces the per-gate wiring snapshots (optionality, scanner, mutation)' — those 3 snapshot tests are deleted in the same diff, so this parametrized node is now the only guard of the invariant
blocking.finding: The rewritten test_optionality_contract_gates_the_verified_path builds its parametrize cases from _verified_lane_reusable_jobs() at collection time with no non-emptiness guard; if that discovery returns an empty list (reusable jobs renamed, the `_`-prefix convention changed, or a YAML/parse change), pytest executes zero cases and the test passes without running, silently dropping the sole owner of the 'every Verified reusable job runs on the patchset, folds into vote.needs, and is shared with a push/PR lane' contract.
scenarios: A future refactor renames the reusable workflows off the `_` prefix or restructures gerrit-verify.yaml's job mapping
A PyYAML/structure change causes `job.get('uses')` to not match for any job
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a standalone sanity test asserting `len(_verified_lane_reusable_jobs()) >= 6` (or == the known count, bumped intentionally), so an empty/under-count discovery fails red instead of yielding an empty parametrize set.
